input: The adsorption of a dye from water onto a metal-organic framework was investigated by means of a series of batch tests carried out at 298 K. The experimental data were fitted to the Langmuir model, and the fitted Langmuir capacity was found to be 239 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 6, which represents a substantial uptake. In a further set of experiments, an adsorbent dose of 0.8 g L-1 succeeded in removing, after a contact time of 120 min, some 87% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1. These results are certainly encouraging as far as the removal of the dye is concerned. It should nevertheless be borne in mind that the Langmuir fit has been reported for pH 6 only, and that the capacity of the material at other pH values was not measured during the course of this work, so that any statements about performance under conditions of different acidity would, at this stage, be speculative. Further investigations would accordingly be needed before the behaviour of the adsorbent across the wider pH range could be characterised with confidence, and the conclusions of the present work should be read with that reservation firmly in mind.
target: Adsorption of a dye from water on a metal-organic framework was measured in batch tests at 298 K. The fitted Langmuir capacity was 239 mg of dye per gram of adsorbent at pH 6. At an adsorbent dose of 0.8 g L-1, removal after 120 min was 87% of the initial dye concentration of 50 mg L-1. The capacity figure and the removal figure describe different things: the capacity is a property of the fitted isotherm at the stated pH, and the removal is the outcome at one dose, one contact time and one initial concentration. A higher dose or a longer contact time would change the removal without changing the capacity, and the two figures cannot be substituted for each other. Both figures were obtained in the setting the batch test fixes: a closed vessel, a stated temperature, and contact between the adsorbent and the solution for the stated time. Nothing in the results addresses flow through a bed, regeneration of the material after use, or competition from other solutes present in a real effluent, and the figures should not be read across to those settings. The Langmuir fit is reported for pH 6 only; capacity at other pH values was not measured. The results therefore establish the material's performance at the stated pH and under the stated test conditions, and they are silent on the pH dependence that a treatment application would need.
